text:
I need to write a reference letter. I manage a 400-cow dairy farm, and one of our workers, Tomás, is applying to the two-year agricultural technology program at the state technical college.

What I know about him:
- He's worked for us for 3 years, since he was 19.
- He runs the 3 a.m. milking shift on his own, 5 days a week.
- He learned our herd management software and now flags sick cows for the vet. Last winter he caught 9 cases of mastitis early.
- He left for 5 weeks in the middle of last summer when his father got sick in Mexico. He told me 2 days before he left.
- His written English is weaker than his spoken English. He's taking a night class for it.
- He has missed 2 shifts in 3 years, not counting those 5 weeks.

One page, from me as farm manager.

Before I draft this, a few questions. The answers will change what goes into the letter:

1. **How did the 5-week absence end?** Did he come back on the date he said, and did you keep his job open for him? I'm thinking of mentioning it briefly and framing it as a family emergency he handled responsibly, but only if that matches what happened. Or would you rather leave it out completely?
2. **How did he learn the herd management software?** Did he teach himself, did you train him, or did he ask to take it on? Also, did the vet or anyone else say anything about the 9 mastitis cases, like money or cows saved? A specific result like that would be the strongest line in the letter.
3. **Do you have a sense of what he wants to do after the program?** For example, come back to your farm, move into herd health, or run his own operation. Would you hire him again or promote him when he finishes?
4. **Should the letter mention his written English and the night class?** The admissions committee may see it in his application essay anyway. If you bring it up first and point to the class, it reads as effort, not a weakness. But it's your call.
5. **Details for the header and signature:** your name, the farm's name and location, Tomás's last name, and the college's name. Is there a specific person or committee to address it to?

If you don't know some of these, just say so. I'll write without them and won't fill in anything you haven't told me.

1. He came back on the day he said he would. Before he left he got his cousin, who used to work for us, to cover his shifts. Mention it the way you said.
2. I don't remember exactly how he learned the software. The vet said catching those mastitis cases early saved us about $8,000.
3. I don't know what he plans after the program. I can keep his job open part-time on weekends while he's in school.
4. Yes, mention it and the night class like you suggested.
5. I'm Mike Hollis, farm manager at Hollis Dairy. He's Tomás Reyes. I don't have a specific person to address it to. It goes in through the college's online portal.

<final_document>
Hollis Dairy

November 16, 2026

To the Admissions Committee, Agricultural Technology Program:

I am the farm manager at Hollis Dairy, a 400-cow operation, and I am writing to recommend Tomás Reyes for your two-year agricultural technology program. Tomás has worked for us for three years, since he was 19. He is one of the most reliable people I have had on this farm.

Tomás runs our 3 a.m. milking shift on his own, five days a week. Nobody is there to check on him at that hour, and I have never needed to. In three years he has missed two shifts.

He also learned our herd management software and now uses it to flag sick cows for our vet. Last winter he caught nine cases of mastitis early. Our vet estimates that saved us about $8,000. Nobody assigned him that work. He took it on, and it has made him more valuable to us than the milking job alone.

Last summer his father became seriously ill in Mexico, and Tomás needed to be there for five weeks. Before he left, he arranged for his cousin, a former employee of ours, to cover all of his shifts. He came back on the day he said he would. He handled a family emergency without leaving the farm short-handed, and I respect him for that.

His spoken English is good. His written English is weaker, and he knows it. He is taking a night class to improve it, on top of a schedule that starts at 3 a.m. I expect he will bring the same effort to your coursework.

We will keep a part-time weekend position open for Tomás while he is in school. I would not do that for someone I did not want back.

I recommend him without reservation. Please contact me if I can tell you more.

Sincerely,

Mike Hollis
Farm Manager, Hollis Dairy
[Phone] | [Email]
</final_document>

I left out several things you didn't give me:

- **How he learned the software and what he plans after school.** You weren't sure about these, so the letter doesn't mention them.
- **College name and farm location.** You didn't give me these. The salutation names only the program, which works for a portal upload. Add the college name or a town and state if you'd like them in.
- **Phone and email.** Fill in the placeholders at the bottom.
- **"Nobody assigned him that work."** Please check this line. I based it on him learning the software and taking on the vet flagging himself. If you trained him or gave him the job, delete that sentence and the rest of the paragraph still works.
